subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should OpenClaw support PowerShell expansion-bearing Windows exec commands through one-shot explicit approval, as proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322, or document them as unsupported inline forms requiring script files?
rationale: Current source shows the approval analysis still rejects `$` expansion syntax, but changing it affects the exec approval/security boundary and the candidate PR is still missing real Windows/Gateway proof.

options.title: Prove and land the one-shot approval path
options.body: Require redacted Windows/Gateway proof for a `$env:*` or `$_` command reaching one-shot explicit approval without auto-review or hanging, then land the candidate fix if the proof holds.

options.title: Document inline PowerShell expansions as unsupported
options.body: Close the implementation direction and update exec docs/tool guidance to steer users to direct PowerShell syntax that is supported or to `.ps1` files for variable-heavy commands.

options.title: Pause for a broader exec contract design
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers define a broader Windows command-fidelity contract covering direct PowerShell, nested wrappers, approval analysis, and docs.

recommendation.title: Prove and land the one-shot approval path
recommendation.body: Require redacted Windows/Gateway proof for a `$env:*` or `$_` command reaching one-shot explicit approval without auto-review or hanging, then land the candidate fix if the proof holds.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision sits on the command authorization planner and Windows shell analysis surface introduced by this owner history.
